question: Centralized maintenance dispatch with scarce heterogeneous passive technicians: planning, learned policies and size generalization

claims.claim_text: Capacity-constrained maintenance and heterogeneous repairman assignment already have analytical and optimization precedents.
Centralized PPO with multiple crews and imitation pretraining predates this project direction.
Quality-compute comparison and graph-based maintenance assignment/size testing have direct precedents.
Learning and planning can be combined; finite rollout is not an exhaustive optimal oracle.
Variable-size neural inputs permit application but do not guarantee scale generalization; explicit constructive and residual-state methods have tested transfer.
Compute accounting must distinguish training, teacher generation, decoding, sampling and search; robust evaluation includes uncertainty and strong solver baselines.
A non-FIFO scarce-skill dispatcher with size/topology transfer is a candidate research question, not proven novelty or RL superiority.
DAgger addresses learner-induced state distribution, but its guarantee does not turn an approximate teacher into a maintenance optimum.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: No first-ever or exhaustive novelty claim; abstract-only unknowns must remain unknown.
Do not call planning or bounded solver references global optimum without certified bounds.
Do not equate MARL labels with decentralized execution or heterogeneous machines with heterogeneous workforce.
Clearly separate project results and proposed hypotheses from published evidence.
